case_title: Ram Singh v. State of U.P.
accused_victim_relationship: Political rival and prior enmity with the informant (the victim's son) over a village Pradhan election; no direct relationship with the deceased is described.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.301 r/w s.302; IPC s.307 (chargesheet also cites s.34 for s.307)
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony; medical (post-mortem) evidence; seizure of cartridge tikli and pellets; police and village-head testimony
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.301 r/w s.302 and s.307 IPC; life imprisonment for s.301/302 and 5 years RI for s.307, concurrent. Co-accused acquitted.
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence confirmed
neutral_facts: On an evening, the victim was sitting on a cot in the open space in front of the family house near the entrance. Her two sons were sitting nearby, and two neighbours sat on another cot. They were chatting under a lantern hanging from the roof. At about 8 pm, the accused arrived from the north with a co-accused. The prosecution alleged that the co-accused told the accused that one son was causing trouble and should be killed. The accused then fired a country-made pistol. The bullet struck the victim's left breast, and she died immediately. The targeted son said he bent below the cot. The witnesses gave differing accounts of where people were sitting and whether the son had stood up. The son lodged a written report at a police station at midnight on the same day, stating that the two men ran away towards the north. The police seized a cartridge tikli from the wound, a 12 bore cartridge from the cot, and 12 pellets from the wound. The post-mortem recovered 55 pellets from the body. The pistol was never recovered. The pellets and tikli were not sent for ballistic examination. Blood-stained clothes and soil samples were sent to a chemical examiner, but no report was received. Another son who was present and the scribe of the report were not examined. A village head said he heard the firing and learned of the death later from a passer-by, who was also not examined. The prosecution case mentions a prior rivalry over a village election and related cross cases.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from a gunshot wound to the left breast, bone-deep, with broken ribs, lung and heart lacerations; 55 pellets removed at post-mortem
motive: alleged: prior political enmity over the village Pradhan election between the accused and the informant; the court did not decide motive
key_evidence_accepted: None accepted as sufficient to prove guilt. Eyewitness evidence was found unreliable; medical evidence of the gunshot wound was noted but did not cure the gaps.
witness_credibility: Eyewitnesses (informant and PW-2) were not found credible: versions of positions and movements were inconsistent; PW-3 said he did not see a pistol; material witnesses were not examined.
post_offence_conduct: As alleged by the prosecution witnesses, the accused and co-accused ran away towards the north after the shooting.
bail_history: Supreme Court issued notice on the prayer for bail; outcome of bail prayer not stated
trial_duration: offence: not given (FIR lodged 19.08.1982 at midnight); trial judgment: 28.05.1983; High Court: 05.02.2018; Supreme Court: 21.02.2024
legal_representation: Accused: Pradeep Kumar Mathur, Chiranjeev Johri, Chandra Nand Jha, M.K. Tiwari, Sitesh Kumar, Arvind Kumar (Advocates). State: Rana Mukherjee, Sr. Adv., Samarth Mohanty, Ankit Goel (Advocates).
investigation_status: FIR registered as No. 252/1982; chargesheet filed; trial held
procedural_irregularity: Material witnesses (the other son and the scribe, and a passer-by) not examined; adverse inference drawn; pellets and tikli not sent for ballistic examination; weapon not recovered; chemical examiner report not received
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted and sentenced. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction confirmed. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, accused acquitted (benefit of doubt).
prosecution_argument: Ocular evidence proves the accused fired the fatal shot; given the gruesome nature of the killing and witness testimony, conviction is justified and the High Court rightly dismissed the appeal.
defence_argument: Eyewitnesses were interested and political rivals and not true eyewitnesses; material witnesses not examined; no weapon recovered and no ballistic link; the co-accused was acquitted on the same evidence, so the accused should also be acquitted; no evidence exists.
legal_principle_applied: Non-recovery of weapon and absence of ballistic expert are not fatal alone, but become fatal where eyewitness evidence is not credible and material witnesses are not examined. Benefit of doubt applies where co-accused with identical evidence was acquitted (parity).
precedent_relied_upon: Javed Shaukat Ali Qureshi v. State of Gujarat, (2023) 9 SCC 164; Munna Lal v. State of U.P. (2023); Gurucharan Singh v. State of Punjab, AIR 1963 SC 340; Sukhwant Singh v. State of Punjab, (1995) 3 SCC 367; State of Punjab v. Jugraj Singh, (2002) 3 SCC 234; Gulab v. State of U.P., (2022) 12 SCC 677; Pritinder Singh v. State of Punjab, (2023) 7 SCC 727
other_sentence_order: Appellant directed to be released from jail forthwith, if not required in any other case
